answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: every agent must lock a real bond in escrow before it can earn, and its rewards vest slowly over many epochs. An attacker may wander across thousands of forged personas, yet each clone still needs funded capital and a reputation history it cannot fake, so none reaches the onyx tier of trusted peers overnight. A shared slashing rule burns every bond in a detected clone cluster, turning the harbor of cheap identities into an expensive liability instead of a hiding place.
